title: Queues
summary: A queue keeps items in the order they arrive. Add items at the back and remove them from the front.
walkthrough: Think of people waiting in line: the next person served is the one who has waited longest. This is called first in, first out (FIFO).
takeaway: Enqueue adds at the tail; dequeue removes from the head.

title: Doubly linked lists
summary: A linked list is made of nodes. Each node stores a value and links to other nodes; a doubly linked node links both forward and backward.
walkthrough: Starting at the head, follow each next link to visit the nodes. A previous link lets you move back to the prior node without searching from the head again.
takeaway: The links determine the order; nodes do not need to sit next to each other in memory.

title: Array storage and free lists
summary: An array can store node fields in numbered slots. A free list links together the slots that are currently unused.
walkthrough: The list head points to the first used slot. The free pointer points to the first empty slot; allocating takes a slot from that chain, while freeing returns a slot to it.
takeaway: Storage location and list order are separate: follow the links to find the logical order.
diagram: used: head → slot 4 → slot 1     free: free → slot 2 → slot 7

title: Rooted trees
summary: A rooted tree starts at one node called the root. Other nodes branch from it, forming parent and child relationships.
walkthrough: In a binary tree, each node has up to two children. A first-child/next-sibling representation can also store a tree where a node has many children.
takeaway: A list follows one chain; a tree branches into parent and child relationships.
